output.content: I walked through the weekly model release cycle with the engineering lead to verify our current operational baseline. When the risk assessment for a new feature set is complete, the analyst prints a summary sheet and physically walks it to the quality assurance lead. The QA lead then reads the printed summary and manually types the corresponding acceptance criteria into the tracking system. There is no electronic link between the two steps. I observed this manual transfer occur for the last three consecutive releases. The time between the risk sign off and the criteria appearing in the system averages four business hours. No automated pipeline exists to move this information. The process relies entirely on the physical presence of the analyst and the manual entry by the QA lead to complete the hand over.
output.reclassify_reason: The text describes observed operational procedures, timings, and the absence of automation without expressing any wishes, refusals, or stated trade-offs.
